reasons: Rule/holding supported: interest 'dissipates when the guest vacates the room'; 'Checkout time is an appropriate marker for the end of a guest's possession... and the resumption of possession by the hotel.'

Timing and facts supported: 'this search happened five hours after checkout time'; officers arrived ~5:20 p.m.; Mendoza 'had not gone to the front desk to check out'; room 'marked... as a checkout'/'vacant.'
Outcome supported: expectation 'not objectively reasonable'; no Fourth Amendment relief without a legitimate expectation of privacy; AFFIRMED.
residual_risks: 'His keycard had been deactivated' is an inference from the hotel's stated walk-out practice ('usually set... to deactivate two hours after checkout'; 'their room keys are deactivated') rather than an explicit case-specific finding; consistent with the record (5+ hrs elapsed) and not a core holding element.
